   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
   268	and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
   269	is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
   270	decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
   271	without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
   272	repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
   273	A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
   274	`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
   275	because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
   276	2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
   277	adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
   278	watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.
   279	
   280	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   281	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   282	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   283	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   284	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   285	
   286	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   287	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   288	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   289	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   290	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   291	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.
   292	
   293	## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`
   294	
   295	`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
   296	`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
   297	`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
   298	proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
   299	branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
   300	validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
   301	(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
   302	
   303	The local translation is:
   304	
   305	| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
   306	|---|---|---|
   307	| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   308	| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   309	| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |
   310	
   311	`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
   312	responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
   313	comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
   314	that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
   315	`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
   316	refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
   317	is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
   318	collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.
   319	
   320	The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
   321	running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
   322	survives as a lint in all three scripts.
   323	
   324	`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
   325	`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
   326	reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
   327	session used one anyway.
   328	
   329	The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
   330	than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
   331	tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
   332	branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).
   333	
   334	## 11. Operating it
   335	
   336	    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
   337	    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
   338	    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch
   339	
   340	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   341	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   342	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   343	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   344	neither publishes a review.
   345	
   346	Artefacts:
   347	
   348	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   349	|---|---|---|
   350	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   351	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   352	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
   353	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |
   354	
   355	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
   356	the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
   357	summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
   358	(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
   359	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
   360	in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
   361	is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
   362	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   363	agreeing is intentional redundancy.
   364	
   365	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
   366	block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
   367	hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
   368	not a verdict.

   370	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   371	
   372	Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".
   373	
   374	* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
   375	  One reviewer session; the cascade
   376	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
   377	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
   378	* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
   379	  comes from a branch of this single repository.
   380	* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
   381	  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
   382	* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
   383	  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
   384	  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
   385	  allow-list only approximated.
   386	* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
   387	  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).

   389	
   390	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   391	
   392	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   393	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   394	
   395	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   396	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   397	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   398	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   399	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   400	   `moot: <reason>`);
   401	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   402	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   403	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   404	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   405	
   406	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   407	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   408	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
   409	
   410	## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)
   411	
   412	The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
   413	every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
   414	change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
   415	sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
   416	so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
   417	earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
   418	published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
   419	and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
   420	from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
   421	review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
   422	`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
   423	are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
   424	change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
   425	patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

   383	   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag

   387	   under [audits/](../audits/).

   389	   format in

   391	   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   392	   public name.
   393	   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)
   394	   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   395	   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   396	   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.
   397

   400	   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   401	   exception policy.

   134	   fix kinds, not one per kind.
   135	3. **The exclusion of sync and audit failures from auto-fix**
   136	   (`autofix.md` §3).
   137	
   138	The guard has one deliberate hole.  `pr-review.yml:69-72` says: *we only want
   139	to review human-authored pushes and the final bot-fix result (detected by
   140	iteration cap)*.  Without that exception, the last fix commit — the one that
   141	ships — is the only commit on the branch nobody ever reviewed.  So `autofix.sh`
   142	calls `review.sh <id> --force-review` once when the cap is reached — after
   143	**releasing its own fix lock** (`release_fix_lock` in `autofix.sh`), because
   144	`review.sh` refuses to run while the branch's fix lock has a live holder and
   145	that holder would otherwise be the very process asking for the review.
   146	`--force-review` is the only way past rung 7.  Do not use it to "just get a
   147	review" of a bot commit; that reopens the cascade one commit at a time.
   148	
   149	## 6. What the reviewer must return
   150	
   151	A single account cannot approve its own pull request, so GitHub's review-state
   152	field carries no authority here (`issues-prs.md` §2): the verdict is a trailer
   153	in the agent's last message (`codex exec -o <file>`), and the contract demands
   154	three things in order:
   155	
   156	1. a `## Findings` section, one line per finding, in exactly this shape:
   157	
   158	       - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Path/File.lean:123` — one-line summary
   159	
   160	   with severity in {`blocker`, `changes`, `advisory`} and `-` in place of
   161	   `path:line` when a finding is not tied to a line; or the single line
   162	   `- none`;
   163	2. a `## Review` section with the prose;
   164	3. as the final line, alone:
   165	
   166	       VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED
   167	
   168	A missing or malformed trailer is **not** an approval: `review.sh` exits 4,
   169	posts a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and keeps the raw output under
   170	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/`.  Nothing in the findings section
   171	is discarded either — a line that does not parse is kept verbatim as a
   172	`changes`-severity finding labelled `unparsed finding:`, and a non-approving
   173	verdict with an empty ledger gets one synthesised finding so the merge gate
   174	still blocks.  Both rules follow the same principle as rung 5: the failure mode
   175	worth engineering against is a review that reads green without having happened.
   176	
   177	## 7. Which reviews run
   178	
   179	* **Code review** always.  `pr-review.yml` ran it as a matrix over
   180	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` (anthropic, deepseek).  Locally the matrix
   181	  collapses to one codex session; a second backend can be added by running
   182	  `review.sh` again with `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL` set, which writes a separate
   183	  per-SHA file only if you also change the file name, so treat multi-provider
   184	  review as unimplemented rather than as a one-liner.
   185	* **Prose review** only when the diff touches `blueprint/`.  On GitHub it ran
   186	  unconditionally on a cheaper tier; gating it on the diff is a local
   187	  cost decision, not a weakening — the prose prompt reviews blueprint ↔ Lean
   188	  equivalence and blueprint prose, and a diff that touches no blueprint file
   189	  has nothing for it to review.  Set `MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL` for the
   190	  cheaper-tier split.
   191	
   192	The failure semantics of the two are deliberately different, and the difference
   193	is inherited: `pr-review.yml:112-131` *fails* the code review when its token is
   194	missing, while `pr-review.yml:202-224` *skips* the prose review in the same
   195	situation.  Locally, a code reviewer that dies without output blocks the PR; a
   196	prose reviewer that dies leaves a warning and the code verdict stands.
   197	
   198	The published verdict takes the **worst** of the two lanes, written verbatim on
   199	the `VERDICT:` line of one exact-head `COMMENT` review (marker
   200	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`): `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED` or
   201	`CHANGES_REQUESTED`.  Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT` too; adverseness lives
   202	in the paired `local-review/summary` status, `success` only for `APPROVED` or a
   203	`COMMENTED` verdict with an empty ledger and `failure` otherwise.  A head with
   204	no review at all simply has no such status, which the merge gate reads as
   205	"not reviewed" rather than as a pass.
   206	
   207	## 8. Concurrency
   208	
   209	| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
   210	|---|---|---|
   211	| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
   212	| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |
   213	
   214	The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
   215	`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
   216	`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
   217	tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
   218	saves a write to a branch that has already moved.
   219	
   220	Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
   221	holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
   222	is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
   223	tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
   224	invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
   225	describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
   226	the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
   227	and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.
   228	
   229	`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
   230	The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
   231	checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
   232	rewritten under it.
   233	
   234	## 9. The findings ledger
   235	
   236	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   237	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   238	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   239	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   240	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   241	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   242	
   243	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   244	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:

368	## 5. Review Checklist
   369	
   370	Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:
   371	
   372	1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   373	   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.
   374	
   375	2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and
   376	   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`
   377	   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.
   378	
   379	3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration
   380	   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from
   381	   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See
   382	   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local
   383	   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   384	   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   385	   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,
   386	   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file
   387	   under [audits/](../audits/).
   388	   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and
   389	   format in
   390	   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).

   392	   public name.
   393	   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)
   394	   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   395	   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   396	   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.
   397	
   398	4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask
   399	   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See
   400	   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   401	   exception policy.
   402	
   403	5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved
   404	   metavariables.
   405	
   406	6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on
   407	   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.
   408	
   409	7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be
   410	   upstreamed to Mathlib?
   411	
   412	8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.
   413	   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the
   414	   relevant arXiv paper(s).
   415	
   416	9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement
   417	   from the blueprint, add `\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\leanok` tags to the
   418	   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public
   419	   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record
   420	   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only
   421	   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal
   422	   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected
   423	   by `\uses{...}`. See
   424	   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).
   425	   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or
   426	   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.
   427	   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,
   428	   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,
   429	   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional
   430	   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before

1	# MIPStarRE-local convention addenda
     2	
     3	The canonical convention documents live in the `lean-conventions` skill of
     4	[texra-ai/texra-lean-skills](https://github.com/texra-ai/texra-lean-skills)
     5	(auto-installed for Claude Code sessions via `.claude/settings.json`; other
     6	agents: clone the repository and symlink the skill directories, per its
     7	README). This file holds only
     8	MIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared
     9	rules never move here.
    10	
    11	## Style (MATHLIB_style)
    12	
    13	### Linter warnings
    14	
    15	Do not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add
    16	broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide
    17	blocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real
    18	maintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.
    19	
    20	Fix the warning at its source whenever possible:
    21	
    22	- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;
    23	- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass
    24	  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;
    25	- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;
    26	- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than
    27	  silencing `linter.flexible`.
    28	
    29	If a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting
    30	exception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably
    31	`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.
    32	Such exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as
    33	the main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.
    34	
    35	## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)
    36	
    37	### Source-faithfulness checks
    38	
    39	For this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean
    40	statement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before
    41	applying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions
    42	`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed
    43	source-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the
    44	corresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.
    45	
    46	Reject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,
    47	repair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,
    48	or arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as
    49	positivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal
    50	encodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when
    51	mathematically load-bearing.
    52	
    53	Reviewers should also inspect `\lean{}` and `\leanok` links.  A source-labelled
    54	blueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction
    55	theorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.
    56	Auxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the
    57	remark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.
    58	
    59	## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)
    60	
    61	### Companion document
    62	
    63	> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
    64	> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the
    65	> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still
    66	> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
    67	> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
    68	> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
    69	> Consult it alongside this file during review.
    70	
    71	### Project paper-realignment protocol
    72	
    73	The canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions
    74	`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as
    75	follows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in
    76	`AGENTS.md`):
    77	
    78	> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
    79	> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
    80	> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be
    81	> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
    82	> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
    83	> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
    84	> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
    85	> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
    86	> conditional helper
    87	> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
    88	> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
    89	> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.
    90	
    91	### Axiom policy
    92	
    93	When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
    94	prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
    95	declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
    96	`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
    97	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
    98	the axiomatic base.
    99	
   100	This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
   101	theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
   102	caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
   103	proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
   104	conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
   105	faithful to the paper.
   106	
   107	### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization
   108	
   109	This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
   110	theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
   111	making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.
   112	
   113	Signs to watch for:
   114	
   115	- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
   116	  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
   117	  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
   118	- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
   119	  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
   120	- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
   121	  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
   122	  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
   123	- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
   124	  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
   125	- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
   126	  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
   127	  incompatible universes)
   128	
   129	When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
   130	this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
   131	scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
   132	progress rather than enabling it.
   133	
   134	### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift
   135	
   136	A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
   137	if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
   138	Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
   139	strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
   140	documented mathematical necessity.
   141	
   142	The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
   143	extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
   144	theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
   145	repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
   146	`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
   147	generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
   148	assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.
   149	
   150	Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
   151	be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
   152	named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
   153	helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
   154	obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
   155	that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
   156	`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
   157	blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.
   158	
   159	Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
   160	for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
   161	strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
   162	bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
   163	to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
   164	tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.
   165	
   166	Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
   167	to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
   168	instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
   169	faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
   170	conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
   171	mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
   172	step of the source proof.
   173	
   174	For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:
   175	
   176	- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
   177	- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
   178	- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
   179	  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.
   180	
   181	### Source-statement proof gaps
   182	
   183	**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
   184	[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
   185	proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
   186	structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
   187	conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
   188	tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.

     3

     6	review per head, and a REST merge behind the exact-SHA guard

     8	they were file writes; now they are ``gh api`` calls, so the suite pins them by
     9	standing a fake ``gh`` in front of the layer.
    10	
    11	The fake is a small Python script this file writes into a tempdir and points
    12	``MIPSTARRE_GH`` at (the override read at ``gh_common.py:57-67``).  It logs
    13	argv+stdin to a spool and answers from a canned route table, so every test here
    14	runs offline, needs no ``gh`` installed, and asserts on the *wire* contract —
    15	the route, the method and the JSON payload — rather than on a mock's call list.
    16	An unmatched route fails the call: a test that forgets to declare one sees it.
    17	
    18	Coverage mirrors the layer's failure modes, one test each: status reduction and
    19	posting, comment/review idempotency and post-failure adoption, prerequisite
    20	edge creation and adoption, reviewer-round history, the merge topology check,
    21	label validation and key-marker adoption, the ``pr_merge.py`` gate ladder

    23	snapshot, and a hygiene check that no live tool still reaches for the retired
    24	registry trees.

    27	from __future__ import annotations
    28	
    29	import ast
    30	import io
    31	import json
    32	import os
    33	import re
    34	import shutil

    36	import sys

    38	import tokenize
    39	import unittest

    41	from unittest import mock

    46	
    47	import gh_common  # noqa: E402

    51	#: Fixed slug so no test depends on the machine's git remotes (gh_common.py:70-86).

    53	HEAD = "a" * 40

    57	#: The fake ``gh``.  Kept as source text rather than a checked-in helper script:

    61	"""Stand-in for the gh CLI: log every call, answer from a canned route table."""
    62	import json
    63	import os
    64	import re
    65	import sys
    66	
    67	argv = sys.argv[1:]
    68	method = argv[argv.index("-X") + 1] if "-X" in argv else "GET"
    69	path = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else ""
    70	rel = re.sub(r"^repos/[^/]+/[^/]+/", "", path)
    71	stdin = sys.stdin.read() if "--input" in argv else ""
    72	spool = os.environ["MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_SPOOL"]
    73	with open(spool, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    74	    handle.write(json.dumps({"argv": argv, "method": method, "path": path,
    75	                             "rel": rel, "stdin": stdin}) + "\\n")
    76	
    77	with open(os.environ["MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_ROUTES"], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    78	    routes = json.load(handle)
    79	state_path = spool + ".state"
    80	used = {}
    81	if os.path.exists(state_path):
    82	    with open(state_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    83	        used = json.load(handle)
    84	
    85	for index, rule in enumerate(routes):
    86	    key = str(index)
    87	    if rule.get("method", "GET") != method or not re.search(rule["path"], rel):
    88	        continue
    89	    if rule.get("once") and used.get(key):
    90	        continue
    91	    used[key] = used.get(key, 0) + 1
    92	    with open(state_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    93	        json.dump(used, handle)
    94	    if rule.get("fail"):
    95	        sys.stderr.write(rule.get("stderr") or "fake gh: canned refusal\\n")
    96	        raise SystemExit(1)
    97	    if "body" in rule:
    98	        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(rule["body"]))
    99	    raise SystemExit(0)

   101	sys.stderr.write("fake gh: no route for %s %s\\n" % (method, rel))
   102	raise SystemExit(1)

   106	class FakeGitHub:
   107	    """A fake ``gh`` binary plus its route table, all inside one tempdir."""

   109	    def __init__(self, tmp: Path) -> None:

   111	        self.binary = tmp / "gh"
   112	        self.binary.write_text(FAKE_GH, encoding="utf-8")
   113	        self.binary.chmod(0o755)
   114	        self.spool = tmp / "gh-calls.jsonl"
   115	        self.routes_path = tmp / "gh-routes.json"
   116	        self.routes: list[dict] = []
   117	        self._flush()
   118	
   119	    def route(self, path: str, body=None, *, method: str = "GET",
   120	              fail: bool = False, once: bool = False) -> "FakeGitHub":
   121	        """Declare one reply.  *path* is a regex against the repo-relative route.
   122	
   123	        Rules match in declaration order, so a ``once=True`` rule in front of a
   124	        broader one models "state changed between two reads" — exactly the
   125	        adoption paths at ``gh_common.py:216-224`` and ``:336-343``.
   126	        """
   127	        rule: dict = {"path": path, "method": method}
   128	        if body is not None:
   129	            rule["body"] = body
   130	        if fail:
   131	            rule["fail"] = True
   132	        if once:
   133	            rule["once"] = True
   134	        self.routes.append(rule)
   135	        self._flush()
   136	        return self
   137	
   138	    def reset(self) -> None:
   139	        """Forget the routes and the call log; used between gate scenarios."""
   140	        self.routes = []
   141	        self._flush()
   142	        for path in (self.spool, Path(str(self.spool) + ".state")):
   143	            if path.exists():
   144	                path.unlink()
   145	
   146	    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
   147	        return {"MIPSTARRE_GH": str(self.binary),
   148	                "MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO": REPO,
   149	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_SPOOL": str(self.spool),
   150	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_ROUTES": str(self.routes_path)}
   151	
   152	    def calls(self) -> list[dict]:
   153	        if not self.spool.exists():
   154	            return []
   155	        return [json.loads(line) for line in
   156	                self.spool.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line]
   157

   164	    def _flush(self) -> None:

   151	A single account cannot approve its own pull request, so GitHub's review-state

   178	
   179	* **Code review** always.  `pr-review.yml` ran it as a matrix over
   180	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` (anthropic, deepseek).  Locally the matrix
   181	  collapses to one codex session; a second backend can be added by running
   182	  `review.sh` again with `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL` set, which writes a separate
   183	  per-SHA file only if you also change the file name, so treat multi-provider
   184	  review as unimplemented rather than as a one-liner.
   185	* **Prose review** only when the diff touches `blueprint/`.  On GitHub it ran
   186	  unconditionally on a cheaper tier; gating it on the diff is a local
   187	  cost decision, not a weakening — the prose prompt reviews blueprint ↔ Lean
   188	  equivalence and blueprint prose, and a diff that touches no blueprint file
   189	  has nothing for it to review.  Set `MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL` for the
   190	  cheaper-tier split.
   191	
   192	The failure semantics of the two are deliberately different, and the difference
   193	is inherited: `pr-review.yml:112-131` *fails* the code review when its token is
   194	missing, while `pr-review.yml:202-224` *skips* the prose review in the same
   195	situation.  Locally, a code reviewer that dies without output blocks the PR; a
   196	prose reviewer that dies leaves a warning and the code verdict stands.
   197	
   198	The published verdict takes the **worst** of the two lanes, written verbatim on
   199	the `VERDICT:` line of one exact-head `COMMENT` review (marker
   200	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`): `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED` or
   201	`CHANGES_REQUESTED`.  Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT` too; adverseness lives
   202	in the paired `local-review/summary` status, `success` only for `APPROVED` or a
   203	`COMMENTED` verdict with an empty ledger and `failure` otherwise.  A head with
   204	no review at all simply has no such status, which the merge gate reads as
   205	"not reviewed" rather than as a pass.
   206	
   207	## 8. Concurrency
   208	
   209	| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
   210	|---|---|---|
   211	| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
   212	| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |
   213	
   214	The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
   215	`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
   216	`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
   217	tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
   218	saves a write to a branch that has already moved.
   219	
   220	Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
   221	holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
   222	is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
   223	tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
   224	invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
   225	describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
   226	the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
   227	and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.
   228	
   229	`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
   230	The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
   231	checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
   232	rewritten under it.
   233	
   234	## 9. The findings ledger
   235	
   236	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   237	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   238	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   239	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   240	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   241	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   242	
   243	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   244	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   246	
   247	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   248	
   249	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   250	|---|---|---|
   251	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   252	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
   268	and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
   269	is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
   270	decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
   271	without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
   272	repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
   273	A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
   274	`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
   275	because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
   276	2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
   277	adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
   278	watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.
   279	
   280	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   281	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   282	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   283	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   284	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   285	
   286	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   287	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   288	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   289	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   290	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   291	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.
   292

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py:450` — isolate the regression subprocess from the documented review kill switch

## Review

The subprocess copies `os.environ` without overriding `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`. With the supported setting `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false`, `review.sh` exits successfully before generating `code-task.md`; the test then fails with `FileNotFoundError`. Since `ci.sh` runs test discovery without clearing this variable, deliberately disabling reviews can make CI fail. Explicitly set the variable to an enabled value or remove review-specific overrides from the child environment.

The production filter otherwise matches `review.md` section 13: carried publications are removed before SHA deduplication and prior-ledger selection. The focused regression and all 14 tests in `test_github_workflow` pass in the default environment; `bash -n` and `git diff --check` also pass.
